She is believed to have been a maiden from Huesca, Spain, who was tortured and executed for her faith during the Roman persecutions of Christians. Her martyrdom is commemorated on January 15.

historical_references.reference: Saint Yacinta of Rome, also known as Sibylla, was a Christian martyr who lived in the 3rd century. She was a member of the Roman aristocracy and converted to Christianity. She was persecuted for her faith during the reign of Emperor Maximian and was tortured and executed, along with several other saints, including Saint Cecilia and Saint Agnes. Her feast day is celebrated on May 7.
